title: Your First Analysis Is the Role You Are Targeting
description: Nine analyst roles compared on the work, the skills, the pay in four countries, the difficulty of entry, and where each one leads.

title: How to Set Up a SQL Database for Beginners
description: Step-by-step beginner guide: set up your first SQL database with SQLite and DB Browser, import a CSV file, and run your first query. Two desktop tools, no server, no install headaches.

title: Git and GitHub for Analysts
description: A beginner-friendly guide to Git and GitHub for data analysts: the everyday save-and-share loop (add, commit, push), starting a repo, publishing a project with GitHub Pages, and fixing the errors that trip everyone up.

title: How to Handle Large Datasets
description: A file too big to open in Excel? Beginner guide to working with large datasets: what counts as large, why a database beats a spreadsheet, indexing, sampling, and the real quirks (zips, data types, disk space) using a 2 GB, 41-million-row example.

title: Data-Driven Thresholds: Picking Cutoffs You Can Defend
description: Every analysis needs cutoffs — minimum reviews, minimum votes, 'active user' definitions. Beginner guide to choosing thresholds from the data instead of guessing: distribution first, price the candidates, defend the pick. Includes the small-sample trap that ruins ratio rankings.

title: Operationalization: Turning Fuzzy Questions Into Measurable Definitions
description: What 'operationalization' and 'operational definition' mean in data analysis: how vague concepts like 'active user', 'churn', or 'popular' become exact, measurable metric definitions — the method, the validity question, and a real worked example.

title: Your Data Is Never Fully Clean, and Analysts Ship Anyway
description: Data cleaning never finishes — professionals ship anyway by documenting limitations. What a limitations section is, the three levels of data-quality accounting (deliverable, working record, quantified), and real examples from open portfolio projects.

title: Why Exploratory Data Analysis Matters
description: What exploratory data analysis (EDA) is, why John Tukey invented it, how Anscombe's quartet and the Datasaurus Dozen prove summary statistics can lie, and what exploration looks like in real portfolio projects — explained for beginners.

title: How SQL and Python Work Together in Data Analysis
description: Beginner guide to how SQL and Python fit together in real analyst work: what each tool is actually for, the collect-analyze-present pipeline, a real example with a live API and SQLite, and which one to learn first.

title: The SQL CASE Expression, Explained for Beginners
description: Beginner guide to SQL CASE WHEN THEN ELSE END: both forms of CASE, why the order of the WHEN clauses changes the answer, why WHEN col = NULL never matches, where a CASE can go in a query, and how analysts use it for cleaning, bucketing, flags and conditional aggregation.

title: Entity Resolution: One Real Thing, Many Messy Names
description: Entity resolution and record linkage explained for beginner analysts: why one artist appears under seven names, how normalization rules get built and tested, match rates, clerical review, and when NOT to merge — a complete worked example on real chart data.

title: COUNT in SQL, Explained for Beginners
description: Beginner guide to SQL COUNT: how COUNT(*), COUNT(column), and COUNT(DISTINCT column) differ, why NULLs make them disagree, how COUNT pairs with GROUP BY, and how analysts use COUNT to verify a data migration and check a real dataset.

title: Technical Tenacity: What to Do When the Tools Fight Back
description: Real data work is a chain of errors, blocks, and mysteries — and working through them is a learnable method, not a personality trait. Four true debugging stories from one working day, the diagnosis loop, and the research on why struggle teaches.

title: How to Build a Tableau Dashboard and Story
description: A beginner's click-by-click guide to building a Tableau dashboard and a three-point story: shape the data, write one rate calculation, build four sheets, assemble the dashboard, sequence the story, and publish it on Tableau Public.

title: SQL JOINs: How to Join Two Tables Without Losing or Doubling Rows
description: Every join concept in the order they build on each other: the pair rule, grain, all six join types, the silent delete, the silent multiply, the two counts that catch each one, and the edge cases that break joins in real data. Worked on 41 million rows.

title: How to Comment SQL So It Teaches
description: A complete format for commenting SQL queries: a boxed WHY header, a read-out-loud block that paraphrases every clause in order, and a clean query with no inline comments. Full before and after, the conventions, and why it works.

title: How to Verify an AI Agent Actually Did the Work
description: An AI agent's report is not evidence, and a tool's success message is not evidence either. What counts as proof, the five checks that catch a false completion, and the measured research on why this happens.

title: SQL Aliases: How to Read a Query Out Loud
description: What AS actually changes, why tables get one-letter nicknames, and the scope rule that makes an alias work in ORDER BY and fail in WHERE. With the literal sentence to say for every shape, and the real error messages.

title: What Is Data Analysis?
description: What data analysis actually is, with a worked example you can follow on paper. Where it gets used, the four steps every analysis uses, what six data jobs really look like day to day, and how to get into the field.

title: Report or Analysis?
description: A report tells you a number. An analysis changes what someone does next. Here is the one-question test that tells them apart, and four moves that turn any report into actionable analysis, with worked SQL.

title: SQL CTEs: How to Build a Query in Steps You Can Check
description: A CTE names one step of a query so you can run it on its own. Here is the WITH syntax, how to stack steps, how to test each one, and why a named step beats a nested subquery. Worked on 82,956 real games.

title: SQL Foundations, Start to Finish
description: Every core SQL idea in the order they build on each other: tables and grain, the six clauses and the order they really run in, NULL, filtering, aggregation, GROUP BY and HAVING, joins, CASE, subqueries, CTEs, window functions, keys and indexes.

title: GROUP BY and HAVING: How to Summarize Rows Without Getting a Fake Answer
description: What GROUP BY actually does to your rows, why WHERE and HAVING are not interchangeable, and the one line that stops a category of eleven records from topping your chart. Worked on 82,956 real games.

title: SQL Window Functions: How to Get the Top Row Per Group
description: A window function adds a number to every row without collapsing any of them. Here is OVER, PARTITION BY, ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, running totals and LAG, worked on a real 175-game list.

title: Tableau Concepts, Start to Finish
description: Every core Tableau idea the Desktop Foundations exam tests, in one pass: dimensions and measures, discrete and continuous, aggregation, joins and blends, the order of operations, calculated fields, LODs, table calculations, sets and parameters, dashboards, actions, and the product family.

title: Tableau Relationships: What the Noodle Actually Does
description: Relationships are the default way Tableau combines tables, and they behave nothing like a join. Here is what the noodle does, why your totals stop inflating, when you still want a join, and the settings that matter.

title: Tableau Sets: What IN and OUT Actually Mean
description: A set does not remove rows. It labels every row IN or OUT so you can compare the two halves. Here is fixed against dynamic, why a set is not a filter or a group, combined sets, and the exam details people miss.

title: The Eight Stages of a Data Migration
description: The eight stages of a data migration end to end: kickoff, profiling, mapping, cleaning, dry run, UAT, cutover and hypercare, with the checkpoint that has to close before the next stage starts.

title: Stage 4: Clean and De-dupe
description: How to clean data before a migration: what to fix by rule, what has to go on an exception list for the client to decide, how to de-duplicate without merging real records, and why the exception list is a gate.

title: Stage 7: Freeze, Cutover, Bridge
description: How to run a data migration cutover: freezing the source system as read only, what staff do during the gap, how a bridge import covers records created mid-migration, and the checks that have to pass before you call it live.

title: Stage 5: The Dry Run
description: How to run a data migration dry run in a sandbox: what to load, the four reconciliation checks that have to pass, how to log issues so the second run is faster, and why manual fixes during a dry run are a failure signal.

title: The Emails That Keep a Migration Moving
description: Email templates for running a client project: the meeting follow up, the stage sign off, the chase, and the handoff. Each one names next actions with dates, links the plan, and asks for confirmation.

title: Stage 3: Map the Fields
description: How to build a field mapping document for a data migration: what each row needs, how to handle fields with no home, why one unique ID ties everything together, and why nothing moves until the map is signed off.

title: Keeping Your Own Files Straight
description: A working file structure for data migration projects: naming that sorts itself, one folder per stage, never overwriting an extract, keeping rejected-row files, and logging bulk loader problems as evidence.

title: Stage 8: Hypercare and Close
description: How to run hypercare after a data migration go-live: what to watch, how long the window should be, the final reconciliation report, the internal readout, and how to hand a client to support without it feeling like abandonment.

title: Stage 1: Kickoff and Scope
description: How to run a data migration kickoff: the four questions that define the project, why the exclusion list matters more than the inclusion list, naming a single point of contact, and the email that closes the gate.

title: What Goes Wrong, and What It Costs
description: The most common data migration failures and what each one costs: duplicates that survive, moves nobody can prove, orphaned documents, silent loader failures, ambiguous dates, and the gap nobody planned for.

title: Stage 2: Profile the Source
description: How to profile a source system before a data migration: the seven checks to run on every extract, what each one tells you about the timeline, and how to turn findings into scope decisions rather than surprises.

title: Ask the Right Questions First
description: The questions to ask before starting a data migration: what success looks like, who signed the contract, who decides on data, what the recovery plan is, and what happens to work created during the migration.

title: When the Client Goes Quiet
description: What to do when a client stops responding during a project: the escalation ladder, why deadlines that come from outside work better than ones you set, when to copy the contract signer, and how to stay defensible if it is ever reviewed.

title: Scope Creep and the Project Plan
description: How to handle scope creep on a client project without saying no: show the impact on the plan, offer to table it or discuss it, route large changes through the people who own the outcome, and keep the timeline honest.

title: Stage 6: User Acceptance Testing
description: How to run UAT on a data migration: give named records rather than open invitations, who should test, how long to allow, what counts as a pass, and how to get a written confirmation without asking for a formal signature.

title: What Data Migration Actually Is
description: Data migration explained for beginners: what the work involves, the vocabulary you will hear in every meeting, the tools it runs on, the eight stages, and the two failures that cost the most.

title: One Migration, Start to Finish
description: A full data migration walked through day by day: eight gates, the emails that closed them, four change requests with what each one cost, and the paper trail at the end.

title: Build a Risk Index That Colors Itself
description: Scored spreadsheets drift because the rule lives in the formatting instead of in a column. Beginner guide to building a composite index in Excel where the score decides the band, the band decides the color, and one edit updates the whole workbook.

title: Build a Dashboard in This Order: Correct, Then Clear, Then Compelling
description: The eight-step order a dashboard gets built in, taken from one Excel build over 82,956 rows of Steam data. Checking the numbers is step four, not step nine.

title: Operations Analytics, Start to Finish
description: Every core operations analytics idea in the order they build on each other: the unit of work, throughput, cycle time, Little's Law, backlog, utilization, first pass yield, service levels and percentiles, and telling a real change from noise.

title: Budget vs Actual Variance Analysis: The Sign Trap and the Percent Trap
description: Variance is actual minus budget, but +$11,800 on a cost line is unfavorable. The F/U convention, the two percent traps, and a worked Excel build with SUMIFS.

title: How to Choose the Right Chart: One Question About Your Data
description: Ask what the reader must compare: categories, time, relationship, or parts. One question, four answers, a decision table, and why a nine-slice pie fails.

title: Correlation vs Causation: The Three Explanations for Any Pattern
description: Ice cream sales and drownings correlate at r = 0.86, until you hold temperature still and it drops to 0.10. The three explanations to say before acting.

title: The Names Came In as Gibberish and Excel Said Nothing
description: Why names import as gibberish: the file was written in UTF-8 and Excel read it as Western European. The signature, the File Origin fix, and why it is data loss.

title: Chart Design Basics: Take Things Away, Then Point
description: Chart design in two moves: delete everything not carrying meaning, then use one accent color to point at the subject.

title: Check Your Work Before Anyone Else Does
description: How to check your work in Excel: when to check, where the check lives, and why you write the expected number down before you look.

title: The Finding That Was Just Your Own Definition
description: The self-audit that catches circular results: could this finding have come out any other way, given how I defined things?

title: The Dialog That Quietly Deletes Your Zip Codes
description: Why Excel turns 08053 into 8053, card numbers into scientific notation, and gene names into dates, and the import habit that stops all three.

title: Show the Unit Without Breaking the Number
description: How to display 21.2x, 2,458k or $1,234.00 while the cell still holds the real number: Ctrl+1, Custom, and the five formats worth knowing.

title: Write the Sentence Your Dashboard Is Arguing
description: A dashboard without a claim is a pile of charts. How to write the finding line, where it goes, and how it becomes the test every chart has to pass.

title: One Row at a Time, or All Rows at Once
description: IF labels one row and fills a column. COUNTIF, SUMIF and AVERAGEIF sweep every row and return one number. Am I labelling or measuring?

title: Four Numbers Across the Top Do More Than Four Charts
description: How to build a dashboard KPI row in Excel: which four numbers earn a spot, why every one is a formula, and how the row tells the story before any chart.

title: Label Your Rows Before You Chart Them
description: How to add a category column in Excel with a nested IF, and why labelling beats filtering: a filter hides rows and loses the comparison, a label keeps every row and makes the chart possible.

title: Name Your Data So Your Formulas Stop Breaking
description: How to turn a range into an Excel Table with Ctrl+T and write structured references. Formulas read like sentences, fill themselves down, and survive new rows.

title: Pick the Chart Your Number Already Decided
description: Comparing groups takes a bar, change over time takes a line, a relationship between two numbers takes a scatter. Say the question's verb and the chart picks itself.

title: Percentages Are the Whole Story and Excel Hides Them
description: How to show percentages in an Excel pivot with Show Values As, and which of the three percent options answers your question.

title: A Pivot Table Is a Question, Not a Report
description: The reframe that makes pivot tables click: Rows is what you group by, Values is what you count. Write the question as a sentence, then place its two halves.

title: Make One Control Drive Every Chart on the Page
description: How to add a slicer and connect it to every pivot with Report Connections: the moment a spreadsheet becomes a dashboard.

title: Sort Your Bar Chart or It Means Nothing
description: An unsorted bar chart hands the ranking work to the reader. Sort descending and the chart answers at a glance. The one exception: categories with a natural order keep it.

title: Excel Just Summed Your ID Numbers and Said Nothing
description: Drop a column into a pivot's Values and Excel picks Sum for anything numeric, including ID codes. The test that catches it, and the ten-second fix.

title: SUMIFS and COUNTIFS: Add Up Only the Rows That Match
description: How to sum only the rows that match your conditions, why SUMIF and SUMIFS put the sum range in opposite places, and the check that catches a wrong total before anyone else does. Every number verified on a 16-row table.

title: pandas GroupBy: How to Summarize a DataFrame Without Losing Track of Your Rows
description: groupby, agg, size vs count, transform, and dropna, worked on one 14-row table. Two rows vanish from the default result, and one line brings them back.

title: Calculated Column vs Measure in Power BI: The Rule That Decides
description: A margin column summed over four rows reports 120% where the real margin is 21.4%. One question decides column or measure, with arithmetic you can check by hand.

title: How to Comment in SQL: -- and /* */, and the Two Traps That Break a Query
description: How to comment in SQL: the two comment syntaxes, where each one goes, the two ways commenting out a line breaks a query, and the comma habit that makes it safe.

title: How to Find Duplicate Rows in SQL (and Decide What Counts as One)
description: The GROUP BY HAVING pattern that lists every duplicate, a ten-second COUNT test for any table, and why analysts mark extras instead of deleting them.

title: Month-over-Month Growth in SQL: LAG, the Growth Formula, and the Traps
description: The MoM growth formula, LAG() in everyday words, and the trap where one skipped month makes SQL report a fake 30.6% drop. Every query run on a real table.

title: NULL in SQL: Why = NULL Finds Nothing and What to Write Instead
description: WHERE assignee = NULL returns 0 of 10 rows, every time. What NULL actually means, IS NULL, the NOT IN trap, COALESCE, and how NULLs quietly move your averages.

title: VLOOKUP vs XLOOKUP: Which One to Use, and How to Switch
description: VLOOKUP has three ways to hand you a wrong value without an error. Here is what each one looks like, how XLOOKUP's arguments remove all three, and when you still need to read VLOOKUP anyway.

title: Which SQL Database Should You Install?
description: File-based engines like SQLite and DuckDB versus servers like PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server. One question decides it.
